Table 1 styles

Richard Aubrey White

Source: vignettes/articles/table1.Rmd
table1.Rmd

pbn::table1() computes the numbers of a descriptive table. A style formats these numbers as the text that a journal or a report needs. With a style, the output gets the columns row, value_pretty and p_pretty. A style can also add a heading row and a Missing row to a variable.

What a style is

A style is a YAML file of pbn, inst/table1/<name>_<YYYY_MM_DD>.yml. Give its name, the file name without .yml, to the argument style of table1(). pbn never edits a released style. A changed style gets a new file with a new date, so a project that names a style gets the same text at each run.

Each field of a style holds a value and a source. The source says where the value comes from. In an installed style, it cites a cell of a real published table or a page of the author guidelines. The section below says how pbn checks this.

The schema

This style file has every field. The section Styles of ?table1 gives the type and the check of each field. These are optional: the section cat, and the fields cont.median_digits, cat.level_prefix, missing.row_template, missing.row_pct_digits and missing.row_label.

bin:
  template: {value: "{events} ({pct})", source: example only}
  pct_digits: {value: 1, source: example only}
cont:
  template: {value: "{median} ({q1}-{q3})", source: example only}
  mean_digits: {value: 1, source: example only}
  sd_digits: {value: 1, source: example only}
  median_digits: {value: 1, source: example only}
cat:
  template: {value: "{events} ({pct})", source: example only}
  pct_digits: {value: 1, source: example only}
  heading_template: {value: "", source: example only}
  level_prefix: {value: "- ", source: example only}
p:
  digits: {value: 3, source: example only}
  template: {value: "P ={p}", source: example only}
  lower: {value: 0.001, source: example only}
  below_template: {value: "P <{lower}", source: example only}
  upper: {value: 0.999, source: example only}
  above_template: {value: "P >{upper}", source: example only}
thousands:
  mark: {value: ",", source: example only}
  from: {value: 10000, source: example only}
missing:
  show: {value: row_if_any, source: example only}
  template: {value: "; {missing} missing", source: example only}
  row_template: {value: "{missing} ({pct})", source: example only}
  row_pct_digits: {value: 1, source: example only}
  row_label: {value: "Missing", source: example only}
footnotes:
  - {value: "Values are n (percent) or median (quartiles).", source: example only}

The fake data below have 12,000 rows in two groups. education is a "cat" variable with three levels and 60 missing values. wide() puts one printed row on each row, with the column label of the output, and one group in each column.

set.seed(1)
n <- 12000
d <- data.table::data.table(
  group = rep(c("Control", "Exposed"), times = c(9000, 3000)),
  smoker = stats::rbinom(n, 1, 0.15),
  age = round(stats::rnorm(n, mean = 31, sd = 5), 1),
  education = factor(
    sample(c("Primary", "Secondary", "Tertiary"), n, replace = TRUE),
    levels = c("Primary", "Secondary", "Tertiary")
  )
)
d$smoker[sample(n, 40)] <- NA
d$education[sample(n, 60)] <- NA
vars <- data.table::data.table(
  var = c("smoker", "age"),
  type = c("bin", "cont")
)
vars_cat <- rbind(vars, data.table::data.table(var = "education", type = "cat"))

# One printed row for each "value", "heading" and "missing" row of the "All"
# group, and the groups in the order of t1.
wide <- function(t1) {
  all <- t1$grp == "All"
  out <- data.frame(row = t1$label[all])
  for (g in unique(t1$grp)) {
    out[[g]] <- t1$value_pretty[t1$grp == g]
  }
  out$p <- t1$p_pretty[all]
  return(out)
}

t1 <- pbn::table1(
  d,
  by = "group",
  vars = vars_cat,
  style = file.path(tempdir(), "example_2026_12_01.yml")
)
knitr::kable(wide(t1))
row All Control Exposed p
smoker 1874 (15.7) 1409 (15.7) 465 (15.6) P =0.839
Missing 40 (0.3) 30 (0.3) 10 (0.3)
age 30.9 (27.6-34.3) 30.9 (27.6-34.3) 31.1 (27.7-34.5)
education P =0.576
- Primary 3965 (33.2) 2982 (33.3) 983 (32.9)
- Secondary 3963 (33.2) 2948 (32.9) 1015 (34.0)
- Tertiary 4012 (33.6) 3022 (33.8) 990 (33.1)
Missing 60 (0.5) 48 (0.5) 12 (0.4) 
attr(t1, "footnotes")
#> [1] "Values are n (percent) or median (quartiles)."

The level rows of education divide by the non-missing count of the group. Its Missing row divides by every row of the group.

How a style is proven

pbn installs a style only with the real published Table 1s whose format it reproduces. Beside each style file inst/table1/<name>.yml is the folder inst/table1/<name>/. For each reference table k, the folder holds five files:

  • reference_<k>.csv: the real table as printed, one string per cell.
  • source_<k>.yml: the authors, the journal, the DOI, the table number, and who transcribed the table from which file.
  • fake_<k>.csv: fake data, one row per fake person. They MUST give every printed row and column, and need not give the printed numbers.
  • vars_<k>.csv: the arguments by and vars of table1(), with the columns label and section of vars.
  • layout_<k>.yml: the printed row and column of each cell of the output. It holds no label.

A test of pbn runs table1(fake, by, vars, style) for each reference table. It compares every printed cell with the cell of the style, the row labels included. A label MUST be the same string. A value cell MUST have the same shape, which is the string with each number masked:

  • The digits before a decimal point collapse to one N. A thousands separator stays, so 12,347 gives N,N.
  • Each digit after a decimal point becomes its own N, so 0.272 gives N.NNN.
  • Every other character stays as printed.

So 397 (27.0%) and 5 (2.8%) share the shape N (N.N%), but 57 (76%) gives N (N%). A style controls the format, and the numbers come from the data.

Each label is the column label of the output of table1(), and never comes from the layout or the reference. A printed row with no computed counterpart MUST be an exception with the rule not_computable. A cell that differs MUST have an entry in the file exceptions.yml of the folder. The entry gives the two strings, a rule, a source and a justification. The rule is one of these:

  • guideline: the reference departs from the author guidelines, and the style follows them. The source gives the page.
  • other_reference: two references disagree, and the style follows the other one. The source cites its cell.
  • not_computable: table1() cannot compute the cell.
  • published_error: the format of the printed cell is wrong, such as a median printed without its value. A wrong number in the right format has the shape of the style, so it needs no exception.
  • author_decision: a named person decided the format, and the style follows the decision. The source MUST be a decision, as below.

The test fails a difference that exceptions.yml does not list. It fails an exception whose strings no longer match those of its cell by the same rule. It fails an exception of a cell that now passes, such as one whose two shapes are now equal. It also fails a style without its folder or with a missing file. A field or an exception whose source says “editorial” fails too. So does a field whose source cites no reference table, no guideline page and no decision.

A decision is a reasoned choice of a named person, in the form decision: <Name>, <YYYY-MM-DD>: <reason>. It MUST have a name, a real date, and a reason of three words or more. Use it only where no reference table and no guideline give the format. The section Styles of ?table1 gives every field of every file.

Withdrawn styles

pbn withdraws a style that it cannot prove. pbn removes its file, and table1() stops on its name with the version that withdrew it and the reason. table1_styles() does not list it. These are the withdrawn styles:

style withdrawn_in reason
ijoa_brief_report_2026_11_20 2026.12.4 it has no reference tables, and 7 of its 18 field sources are an editorial choice

The installed styles

The tables below show smoker and age only. A style without the section cat cannot format a "cat" variable.

ijoa_brief_report_2026_11_21

row All Control Exposed p
smoker 1874 (15.7%) 1409 (15.7%) 465 (15.6%) 0.839
Not recorded 40 30 10
age 31 [28–34] 31 [28–34] 31 [28–34]

Data are presented as number (percentage) or median [first–third quartile].

P values from Pearson’s chi-squared test without continuity correction, or from Fisher’s exact test when an expected count is below 5.
